title: Why a Hotter Pan Can Make Water Last Longer
description:
Why can a hotter pan make a drop of water last longer?

In the Leidenfrost effect, rapid vapor formation beneath the drop creates a cushion. The liquid loses direct contact with the metal, so heat must cross a poorly conducting gas layer.

This is conditional: the surface and drop matter. Hotter does not always mean a longer lifetime; above the transition, more heat can speed evaporation again.

Original qualitative illustration with synthetic narration. The vapor gap is enlarged for clarity; this is not recorded laboratory footage.

Sources:
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4055890/
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6499590/
https://www.reed.edu/physics/332/pdf/Leidenfrost.pdf

firstComment: There is no single transition temperature for every surface and drop. Above the transition, extra heat can increase evaporation again. Primary sources are linked in the description.
